facts.content: Patient has right knee pain with clicking, decreased running tolerance, and episodic tingling in the right toes.
facts.source_text: CC: R knee pain with clicking; dec running tolerance; episodic tingling R toes

facts.content: Symptoms started approximately 2 weeks ago and worsen with longer runs.
facts.source_text: Onset: ~2 wks ago; worsens with longer runs

facts.content: Patient is marathon training, running 4–8 miles, with pain starting about 20 minutes into the run (approximately 2.5–3 miles).
facts.source_text: Marathon training; runs 4–8 miles; pain starts ~20 min into run (~2.5–3 miles)

facts.content: Right knee pain is mainly central, sometimes extending to the right side; intermittent swelling after the first run resolved with ice.
facts.source_text: R knee pain mainly central, sometimes to right side; intermittent swelling after first run resolved with ice

facts.content: Clicking especially occurs with gym activities involving knee flexion to extension.
facts.source_text: Clicking esp with gym “abs” movements involving knee flex→extend

facts.content: No locking, giving way, or instability reported.
facts.source_text: No locking, no giving way, no instability

facts.content: No pain experienced with stairs or walking; able to fully flex and extend the knee.
facts.source_text: No pain with stairs, walking; can fully flex/extend

facts.content: One episode of tingling in the right toes after a run, which resolved with no color or temperature change, and no calf pain.
facts.source_text: One episode tingling R toes after run; resolved; no color/temp change; no calf pain

facts.content: Patient is farsighted.
facts.source_text: PMH: Farsighted

facts.content: Patient had a prior severe urinary tract infection evaluated in the emergency room.
facts.source_text: prior severe UTI evaluated in ER

facts.content: Patient is active and training for a marathon.
facts.source_text: SH: Active; marathon training

facts.content: Patient occasionally smokes cannabis.
facts.source_text: occasional cannabis (smokes a joint)

facts.content: Patient uses ibuprofen up to 400 mg as needed.
facts.source_text: Meds: Ibuprofen up to 400 mg PRN

facts.content: Patient uses Aleve (naproxen) as needed.
facts.source_text: Aleve (naproxen) PRN

facts.content: Patient takes vitamin D.
facts.source_text: vitamin D

facts.content: Patient uses melatonin as needed.
facts.source_text: melatonin PRN

facts.content: Patient uses Xanax as needed for sleep.
facts.source_text: Xanax PRN for sleep

facts.content: The assessment includes a right knee overuse injury likely due to patellofemoral pain syndrome or meniscal irritation.
facts.source_text: 1) R knee overuse injury—likely patellofemoral pain syndrome vs meniscal irritation

facts.content: Episodic right toe paresthesia post-run is transient and likely exertional or positional.
facts.source_text: 2) Episodic R toe paresthesia post-run—transient; likely exertional/positional

facts.content: Intermittent NSAID use for analgesia, but patient requests a stronger anti-inflammatory.
facts.source_text: 3) Analgesic use—intermittent NSAIDs; requests stronger anti-inflammatory

facts.content: Activity modification advised: temporarily reduce or hold running, cross-train with low impact exercises, and avoid painful activities and gym movements provoking clicking.
facts.source_text: Activity modification: Temporarily reduce/hold running; cross-train low impact; avoid painful activities and gym movements provoking clicking.

facts.content: RICE: Continue ice after activity, consider a short course of compression and relative rest.
facts.source_text: RICE: Continue ice after activity; consider short course compression and relative rest.

facts.content: Prescribe a stronger NSAID to start regularly with food and avoid concurrent ibuprofen or naproxen.
facts.source_text: Meds: Start prescribed stronger NSAID regularly with food; avoid concurrent ibuprofen/naproxen

facts.content: Referral to physiotherapy for comprehensive knee assessment including gait analysis, strengthening, and biomechanics evaluation, with consideration of imaging if symptoms persist.
facts.source_text: Referral: Physiotherapy for comprehensive knee assessment, gait/strengthening (quad/hip), biomechanics; consider imaging if persistent sx or exam suggests internal derangement.

facts.content: Safety-net instructions provided: urgent review if persistent or worsening symptoms include swelling, heat, redness, fever, inability to flex or extend, mechanical locking, instability or neurovascular changes.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: Urgent review if persistent/worsening swelling, heat, redness, fever, inability to flex/extend, mechanical locking, instability/giving way, or neurovascular changes.

facts.content: Schedule an in-clinic exam if there is a long wait for physiotherapy and reassess response to NSAID and activity modification.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: If physio wait long, schedule in-clinic exam; reassess response to NSAID and activity modification.
